text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.

- The popularity of Portuguese Prime Minister Antonio Guterres and the ruling Socialist Party has fallen, according to a poll by Publico newspaper and state broadcaster RTP-Antena 1. The opposition centre-right Social Democratic Party and its leader, Marcelo Rebelo de Sousa, have risen in popularity.

- Former Portuguese president Mario Soares will be elected president of the European Movement today. He told the paper in an interview that he believes a federal Europe should have a big say in world affairs.
- Tavares Moreira, chairman of Caixa Central de Credito Agricola, an agricultural bank, has reported a 1996 profit of 5.8 billion escudos, which reflects efforts to restructure the bank's activities.
- Health Minister Maria de Belem has decided to boost controls over the prescription of drugs in a bid to combat fraud.

- Belmiro de Azevedo, chairman of the Sonae group, has bought 3.2 percent of BPI-Banco Portugues de Investimento for six billion escudos, via his private holding Figeste. The deal may be linked to synergies between BPI and Sonae.
- Sonae chief Belmiro de Azevedo has bought 3.5 percent of BPI via his holding Capital Privado.

- The government will bring forward the sale of a 10 percent tranche of Portugal Telecom as part of the third phase privatisation of 26 percent of the telecommunications operator, a Finance Ministry source said. The paper gave no date for the sale of the stake.
